shared_context: Consumer query: definition and overview of blepharitis (eyelid inflammation)

atoms.1: Blepharitis is a chronic inflammatory process of the eyelid margins.
atoms.2: Blepharitis can affect individuals of any age.
atoms.3: Blepharitis is characterized by symptoms such as burning sensation, irritation, tearing, photophobia, blurred vision, and red eyes.
atoms.4: Symptoms of blepharitis include burning sensation.
atoms.8: Symptoms of blepharitis include blurred vision.
atoms.9: Symptoms of blepharitis include red eyes.
atoms.10: Blepharitis may be classified into two subtypes based on the anatomic location: anterior and posterior.
atoms.11: Blepharitis may be categorized based on symptom duration as either acute or chronic.
atoms.12: The exact pathogenesis of blepharitis is not fully understood.
atoms.13: Blepharitis is thought to be caused by bacterial colonization.
atoms.14: Staphylococcus aureus is a bacterium that may cause blepharitis.
atoms.15: Staphylococcus epidermidis is a bacterium that may cause blepharitis.
atoms.16: Blepharitis may be caused by meibomian gland dysfunction.
atoms.17: Other contributing factors to blepharitis include allergens.
atoms.18: Other contributing factors to blepharitis include parasitic infestations.
atoms.19: Demodex mites are parasites that may contribute to blepharitis.
atoms.20: Common systemic associations with blepharitis include rosacea.
atoms.21: Common systemic associations with blepharitis include seborrheic dermatitis.
atoms.22: Diagnosis of blepharitis is primarily based on clinical features.
atoms.23: There are no specific diagnostic laboratory tests for blepharitis.
atoms.24: Treatment of blepharitis involves long-term eyelid hygiene.
atoms.25: Treatment of blepharitis may include topical antibiotics.
atoms.26: Treatment of blepharitis may include systemic antibiotics.
atoms.27: The choice of antibiotics for blepharitis depends on the underlying cause and severity of the condition.
atoms.29: If left untreated, blepharitis can lead to permanent alterations of the eyelid margin.

snippets.output: Blepharitis is a chronic inflammatory process of the eyelid margins and can affect individuals of any age.
Blepharitis is characterized by symptoms such as burning sensation, irritation, tearing, blurred vision, and red eyes.
snippets.notes: Umbrella symptom claim + individual true symptoms merged (Patterns A/C). Photophobia split out (Pattern E) due to differing annotator label.
Photophobia is not a hallmark symptom of blepharitis (more typical of keratitis/uveitis). Annotator labeled false; honored. Split per Pattern E (same-topic-different-fact).

snippets.output: Blepharitis may be classified into two subtypes based on anatomic location (anterior and posterior), and can also be categorized by symptom duration as either acute or chronic.
snippets.notes: Two parallel classification schemes merged (Pattern A).

snippets.output: The exact pathogenesis of blepharitis is not fully understood; however, it is thought to be caused by bacterial colonization (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus, Staphylococcus epidermidis) or meibomian gland dysfunction.
snippets.notes: Premise (uncertain pathogenesis) + proposed mechanisms with specific examples merged (Patterns A/C).

snippets.output: Other contributing factors include allergens and parasitic infestations such as Demodex mites.
snippets.notes: Contributing factors + Demodex specification merged (Patterns A/C).

snippets.output: Common systemic associations with blepharitis include rosacea and seborrheic dermatitis.
Diagnosis of blepharitis is primarily based on clinical features, as there are no specific diagnostic laboratory tests.
snippets.notes: Diagnostic conclusion + supporting premise merged (Pattern C).

snippets.output: Treatment involves long-term eyelid hygiene and may include topical or systemic antibiotics depending on the underlying cause and severity of the condition.
Although blepharitis is not sight-threatening, it can lead to permanent alterations of the eyelid margin if left untreated.
